Indian Ocean yellowfin tuna (simulated) assessment data

io_yft_data.Rd

Model inputs for a quarterly, single-region assessment of simulated Indian Ocean yellowfin tuna, converted from the IATTC analyst team's Stock Synthesis 3 (SS3) model for the Spatial Stock Assessment Simulation Experiment (replicate 4). Used by the Indian Ocean yellowfin cross-model comparison article (vignette("io-yft-ss3-comparison", package = "opal")).

Usage

io_yft_data

Format

A named list of 62 elements in the form opal_obj() expects: dimensions, catch (catch_obs_ysf), the index (cpue_data), biology, growth settings, length compositions (lf_*), the recruitment bias adjustment (bias_adj_y) and priors.

Source

Converted from SS3 v3.24 files with the SS3-to-opal converter in https://github.com/N-DucharmeBarth/opal-sandbox (code/rtmb/scripts/04-export-io-yft-for-opal.r). SS3 model by M.N. Maunder, H. Xu and C. Minte-Vera (IATTC); data simulated from the operating model described in Goethel et al. (2024) doi:10.1111/faf.12819 .

Details

The model runs 256 quarterly time steps (n_year = 256, n_season = 1) and SS3 ages 1–28, so the opal age index equals the SS3 age. There are 20 fisheries: 16 extraction fleets with catch in numbers, and the longline CPUE index split into four quarterly series (fisheries 17–20), each with its own catchability. Length compositions (5 cm bins) are multinomial for fisheries 1–14 and 16, with SS3's mult_by_lencomp_N carried as lf_var_adjust; prep_lf_data() has already been applied.

Biology is SS3's age-based end-of-run biology: M, weight, maturity and spawning potential at age, with M scaled to the quarter. Growth uses SS3's GrowthModel 3 (age-specific K): k_mult_ages gives the ages with K multipliers, which are in io_yft_parameters$log_k_mult, and growth_plus_group_adjust applies SS3's plus-group length approximation. Selectivity is length-based (sel_type_f: 2 = double normal for fisheries 1–16, 1 = logistic for the index series). sel_basis_f is not set, so every curve is evaluated on length; adding sel_basis_f = rep(2L, 20) evaluates them on age instead, as SS3 does (see the cross-model comparison article). priors holds the default priors from get_priors().

See also

io_yft_parameters, io_yft_map, io_yft_reference

Examples

data(io_yft_data)
io_yft_data$n_year
#> [1] 256
head(io_yft_data$cpue_data)
#>   year month  ts fishery index metric units    value        se
#> 1   81     2  81      17     1   cpue     2 1.399491 0.0628665
#> 2   85     2  85      17     1   cpue     2 1.244067 0.1169320
#> 3   89     2  89      17     1   cpue     2 1.235876 0.0581591
#> 4   93     2  93      17     1   cpue     2 1.201179 0.0749399
#> 5   97     2  97      17     1   cpue     2 1.194558 0.0583808
#> 6  101     2 101      17     1   cpue     2 1.261683 0.1402180
